Zhuravnyky Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Zhuravnyky's Jewish population is first mentioned in the second half of the 17th century, with a wooden synagogue built by the 18th century and rebuilt in 1865; the community, divided between Olyka and Trisk Hasidic movements, reached 870 (64.9 percent) by 1897. A Jewish self-protection group formed in 1918, though the community still suffered a pogrom led by Polish army units in 1920. In October 1941, Jews were deported to the ghetto in Horokhiv, where about 500 were murdered on September 4, 1942; a monument was erected in 2005.
